title: Breakthrough Advertising (Eugene Schwartz, 1966; current hardcover reprint)
publisher: Titans Marketing (Brian Kurtz), the book's rights holder
supports: The book and its 1966 date; source of the awareness and market sophistication ideas summarised in the canon

title: Scientific Advertising (Claude C. Hopkins, 1923 text)
supports: Hopkins's book (Dover republication of the 1923 edition): measurable selling, specificity, samples and testing

title: Ogilvy on Advertising (David Ogilvy)
supports: Ogilvy's book: research, effective copy and what makes advertising work

title: Tested Advertising Methods (John Caples, first published 1932)
supports: Bibliographic record of Caples's book, first published 1932, later Prentice-Hall editions; source of the tested-headline ideas

title: The Adweek Copywriting Handbook (Joseph Sugarman)
supports: Sugarman's handbook (January 2007 edition): copy process and the psychology of buying

title: The 7 Principles of Persuasion
supports: The seven principles (reciprocity, scarcity, authority, consistency, liking, social proof, unity) and the emphasis on ethical use

title: Demand-Side Sales 101: Stop Selling and Help Your Customers Make Progress (Bob Moesta)
supports: Moesta's book applying Jobs to be Done to buying and selling: customers buy to make progress

title: Unpacking the Progress Making Forces Diagram (Jobs-to-be-Done Radio)
publisher: Jobs to be Done / The Re-Wired Group
supports: Bob Moesta and Chris Spiek's definitions of the four forces: push, pull, anxiety, habit

title: Review Mining for Customer Research and Sales Marketing (Joanna Wiebe, 2014)
supports: The message-mining method and the Beachway test: more than 400% more button clicks and more than 20% more lead form submits

title: 7 copywriting research techniques conversion copywriters love (2022)
supports: Research methods: interviews, surveys, review mining, heatmaps, thank-you polls, analytics, competitor audits

title: How to Use Voice of Customer Research to Boost Conversions
supports: Voice-of-customer research as the basis for conversion copy (site blocks automated fetching; page confirmed in search results)

title: #5: Learning From Customers (Qualitative Surveys)
supports: Survey recent first-time buyers, use open-ended questions, aim for at least about 100 responses (site blocks automated fetching; page confirmed in search results)

title: How Users Read on the Web (Jakob Nielsen, 1997)
supports: 79% scanned, 16% read word by word; concise 58%, scannable 47%, objective 27%, combined 124% better usability

title: How Little Do Users Read? (Jakob Nielsen, 2008)
supports: Users read at most about 28% of words per page visit, likely about 20%; sample and caveats

title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web: Misunderstood, But Still Relevant (Even on Mobile) (Kara Pernice, 2017, reviewed 2026)
supports: F-pattern and other scanning patterns; front-loading, meaningful headings, descriptive links

title: 2024 Conversion Benchmark Report
supports: Median landing page conversion 6.6% (41K+ pages, 464M+ visitors, 57M+ conversions); grade 5-7 copy 11.1% vs 5.3% professional level; correlation caveats

title: The Surprising Power of Online Experiments (Ron Kohavi and Stefan Thomke, Sept-Oct 2017)
supports: Bing ad headline display test: about 12% more revenue, over $100M a year in the US; ideas are hard to value without testing; check surprising results

title: Obama's $60 million dollar experiment (Dan Siroker, 29 November 2010)
supports: 24-combination splash page test; Learn More plus family image raised sign-ups from 8.26% to 11.6% (40.6%); $60M is an extrapolation

title: Organ Donor Register (GDS blog, 18 March 2014)
supports: Eight calls to action tested on over 1,000,000 visitors; reciprocity message won; projected 96,000 extra registrations a year

title: How Not To Run an A/B Test (Evan Miller, 18 April 2010)
supports: Peeking inflates false positives (26.1% in the worked example); fix sample size in advance; n = 16 p(1-p) / delta squared

title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Kohavi, Tang, Xu, 2020)
supports: Standard practical guide to running A/B tests

title: Federal Trade Commission Announces Final Rule Banning Fake Reviews and Testimonials (14 August 2024)
supports: The six practices the rule bans, including AI-generated fake reviews; civil penalties for knowing violations

title: Trade Regulation Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials, 89 FR (22 August 2024)
supports: 16 CFR Part 465; effective date 21 October 2024; AI-generated reviews covered

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Typical-results disclosure for atypical testimonials; disclosing material connections; cherry-picking or suppressing reviews can mislead

title: Federal Trade Commission Announces Updated Advertising Guides to Combat Deceptive Reviews and Endorsements (29 June 2023)
supports: Date and scope of the 2023 Endorsement Guides update: review manipulation, incentivised and employee reviews, clear and conspicuous

title: FTC Report Shows Rise in Sophisticated Dark Patterns Designed to Trick and Trap Consumers (15 September 2022)
supports: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light: disguised ads, fake limited-time countdowns, hard cancellation, buried terms and junk fees, data tricks

title: CMA to boost consumer and business confidence as new consumer protection regime comes into force (7 April 2025)
publisher: UK Competition and Markets Authority, GOV.UK
supports: DMCC Act consumer regime: CMA direct enforcement, fines up to 10% of global turnover, explicit bans on fake reviews and drip pricing

title: Fake reviews (CMA208), published 4 April 2025
publisher: UK Competition and Markets Authority, GOV.UK
supports: CMA guidance on how businesses must comply with consumer protection law on reviews

title: It's the final countdown... but is it really? (20 April 2023)
supports: Countdown timers must reflect real time limits; the offer ends at zero; timers must not restart

title: Online Choice Architecture: How digital design can harm competition and consumers (5 April 2022)
publisher: UK Competition and Markets Authority, GOV.UK
supports: CMA discussion paper and evidence review linking interface design practices and dark patterns to consumer harm
